The men are positioned behind the fish, smiling at the camera. The background shows murky water and part of a boat or dock structure.

selected_experts.reason: Primary class verification: must confirm taxonomic identity at species/subspecies level given morphological ambiguities.
Audit fin-body connectivity and scute row continuity; detect fusion or floating parts missed by visual inspection.
Holistic quality check for subtle distortions, especially around human-fish interaction zones and water reflections.
Verify spatial grounding: ensure fish is physically plausible in relation to holders and water plane; detect depth bleeding.
Attempt to localize barbels and scute rows even if visually ambiguous; provide BBox priors for topology auditor.

focus_areas: Mouth and barbel visibility under low resolution
Scute row definition vs. general skin texture
Human-hand/fish contact boundaries for fusion artifacts
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Prioritize structural plausibility over aesthetic fidelity. If scutes or barbels are not resolved, do not assume absence — consider imaging limitations. However, any sign of limb fusion or impossible anatomy (e.g., symmetric tail if visible) should heavily penalize artifact score. Cross-validate classifier output against known sturgeon subspecies traits (e.g., lake vs. white sturgeon). Pay special attention to whether the 'lighter ventral surface' transitions naturally or shows abrupt cutoffs indicative of segmentation errors.
